Eloise K.: Quick check-in: I finished a mixed-quant bring-up for hummingbird-12b on the doc-summarize + longform slices. Huge perf upside but some targeted quality regressions. Posting numbers and a routing idea.
Marco D.: love it, drop the key deltas pls.
Eloise K.: slice=doc-summarize-1k (avg 980 tokens). Baseline fp16 Rouge-L=47.0 / BERTScore=0.910. mixed-int6/int4 (layer-split) Rouge-L=45.2 / BERTScore=0.901. p95 latency fp16=920ms -> mixed=430ms. throughput +2.5x. cost/1k tokens fp16=$0.078 -> mixed=$0.039.
Yara N.: that's ~50% cost reduction for that traffic. Hallucination / failure modes?
Eloise K.: auto-eval n=1000: mean Rouge-L drop = 1.8 pts (sd 0.9). Hallucination flagged 7/1000 (0.7%) vs fp16 2/1000 (0.2%). Failures concentrated in long legal-doc-summary and chain-of-reasoning items where the model drops clauses. Not random fabrications, mostly omissions and flattened structure.
Marco D.: Product: legal_doc and contract_review cannot accept >0.3% hallucination. Creative/ideation slices can tolerate this.
Eloise K.: I ran a small per-intent sensitivity scan. For creative and FAQ intents, Rouge-L drop ~1.0 and hallucination ~0.2%. For legal_doc and contract_review, Rouge-L drop ~3.1 and hallucination ~1.6%. So we should gate sensitive intents.
Yara N.: What about dynamic quant by token-length or by prefix cache hits? Any cheap heuristic to push risky queries to fp16?
Eloise K.: Yes, two cheap signals worked well in small samples: (1) thread_turns > 7 OR last_user_tokens > 350 -> prefer fp16; (2) low prefix_cache_hit_rate (<40%) correlates with bigger drops since the model loses context benefits. Also a tiny discriminator using normalized logit gap < 0.12 caught ~60% of risky cases.
ops-bot: Auto-eval snapshot (live holdback n=200): mixed mean Rouge-L drop=1.9 (sd 0.8). hallucination flagged 2/200 (1.0%) -> manual triage confirmed 1/200 (0.5%).
Eloise K.: Draft routing prototype:
```yaml
route: doc-summarize
rules:
  - if intent in [legal_doc, contract_review] then model: hummingbird-12b-fp16
  - elif (thread_turns > 7 or last_user_tokens > 350) then model: hummingbird-12b-fp16
  - elif prefix_cache_hit_rate < 0.4 then model: hummingbird-12b-fp16
  - elif logit_gap < 0.12 then model: hummingbird-12b-fp16
  - else model: hummingbird-12b-mixedquant
fallback: hummingbird-12b-fp16
metrics: rouge_l, bertscore, hallucination_rate_by_intent, cost_delta, prefix_cache_hit_rate
```
Marco D.: Nice. What's the econ if we route 40% traffic to mixedquant with those heuristics?
Eloise K.: Baseline site tokens/month ~140M. Raw infra saving for 40% -> mixed reduces cost by ~$17.0k/mo. Accounting for expected extra escalations using observed per-intent misroute rates ~ $3.8k/mo and QA overhead ~$1.2k/mo net ~= $12.0k/mo. If discriminator improves false-negative catch by 50% net ~+$14.5k/mo.
Yara N.: Product asks: (1) 1% fp16 holdback for drift; (2) daily auto-eval + weekly human sample focused on legal_doc; (3) rollback triggers: hallucination_rate > 0.5% for legal_doc over 6h OR rouge_l drop > 1.5 pts sustained 12h.
Eloise K.: Agreed. Canary plan: 48h 5% non-sensitive -> 7d ramp to 40% with 1% fp16 holdback, daily auto-eval and per-intent dashboards. I'll publish a GTN note, reproducible eval notebook, and a cost sheet. Link (internal): https://go/redwood/hbird12b-mixedquant.
Marco D.: I'll add dashboard panels and a feature flag. Please tag me when the canary starts so I can watch the rollback alerts.
Yara N.: Add compliance signoff before enabling for any legal intents. If discriminator + heuristics reach the expected reduction we'll consider widening to 60%.
Eloise K.: Will do. Launching the canary in ~30m. Will post interim auto-eval snapshots here. :rocket:
